memory_update.text: NNI is the primary underfollowed candidate for the student-loan servicing/payment-rails node because it has explicit Loan Servicing and Systems plus Education Technology Services and Payments segments.
FLYW belongs in the discovery lane as an education-payment workflow and tuition-receivables infrastructure provider rather than a generic payments company.
MMS is an underfollowed federal student-loan servicing infrastructure candidate via Aidvantage, but exposure must be sized relative to the broader government-services portfolio.

The likely chokepoints in this node are not physical inputs but regulated servicing licenses/relationships, borrower-account data migration, compliance systems, payment reconciliation, university ERP/accounts-receivable integrations, and federal contract access.

Layer 2 should verify customer concentration, contract duration, margin quality, complaint/remediation risk, and whether education-payment or student-loan servicing revenue is large enough to matter for each candidate.

node: Student-loan servicing, education payments, and compliance infrastructure
summary: Expanded the universe around regulated student-finance operating infrastructure rather than obvious online-learning operators. The strongest underfollowed lane candidates are Nelnet for direct loan servicing plus education payments, Flywire for university tuition/payment workflow infrastructure, and Maximus for federal student-loan servicing via Aidvantage. SLM is included as a reference/private-student-loan anchor because it is directly exposed to origination/servicing economics but is less of a pure third-party infrastructure supplier. This pass emphasizes scarce regulated relationships, compliance-heavy servicing systems, payment rails, borrower/account workflows, and government or university switching friction. No buy/sell recommendation is implied.
